title: A Reusable Semantic Web Framework for Evidence-Grounded Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments under the EU AI Act
abstract: arXiv:2609.39537v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The EU AI Act (Art. 27) requires deployers of high-risk AI systems to conduct Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments (FRIAs) before deployment, yet the evidence needed for credible assessments is fragmented across incompatible incident repositories, risk vocabularies, and legal texts. We present a reusable Semantic Web-based framework that consolidates this evidence for two high-risk public sector categories: employment and worker management (Annex III(4)) and access to essential public services (Annex III(5)(a)). A curated 150-record corpus is annotated along four axes using keyword, LLM, and hybrid methods and serialised as a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph of 1,351 RDF triples. Five FRIA demonstration scenarios surface 103 records (68.7% coverage). translated_title: 《欧盟人工智能法案》下基于证据的基本权利影响评估的可复用语义网框架
translated_abstract: 欧盟《人工智能法案》（第27条）要求高风险人工智能系统的部署者在部署前开展基本权利影响评估（FRIA），然而可信评估所需的证据却分散在不兼容的事件库、风险词汇表和法律文本之中。我们提出了一个可复用的基于语义网的框架，为两个高风险公共部门类别整合这些证据：就业与劳动者管理（附件三第4条）以及基本公共服务的获取（附件三第5条第a项）。一个精选的150条记录语料库采用关键词、大语言模型（LLM）及混合方法沿四个维度进行标注，并序列化为一个包含1,351个RDF三元组、可通过SPARQL查询的知识图谱。五个FRIA演示场景共检索出103条记录（覆盖率68.7%）。基于69条记录黄金标准的评估显示，就业领域的LLM辅助分类仅达到κ = 0.045，这对自动化公平性相关评估而言是一个值得警惕的结果。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个可复用的语义网框架，通过可SPARQL查询的知识图谱整合欧盟AI法案下基本权利影响评估所需的分散证据，同时揭示LLM辅助分类在就业领域的可靠性有限（κ=0.045），为自动化公平性评估敲响警钟。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a reusable Semantic Web framework that consolidates fragmented evidence for Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments under the EU AI Act into a SPARQL-queryable knowledge graph, while revealing cautionary limitations of LLM-assisted classification in the employment domain (κ = 0.045).
